§ 2Content

Indian Dance Forms

Indian dance forms can be divided into two types:

  1. 1. Classical Dance Forms: They have particular steps that need to be performed in particular events (mostly performed in temples).
  2. 2. Folk Dance Forms: No particular steps are defined. They are performed in a specific ritual.

Classical Dance Forms

  • There are 8 classical dances according to Sangeet Natak Akademi (HQ: New Delhi); however the Ministry of Culture recognises 9 classical dances (8 classical dances + Chhau).
  • Origin: Rooted in Natya Shastra (considered as Fifth Veda), written by Bharat Muni.
  • Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikeshvara describes expressions, movements, and gestures.
  • Nritta: Pure form of dance.
  • Nritya: Expressive form of dance (pure dance + expression).

Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu)

  • It is the oldest classical dance of India that is performed solo (by a single person) → known as Ekaharya.
  • Earlier Names: Sadirattam, Thevarattam, Parathaiyar Attam.
  • Bharatanatyam was earlier also known as Dasiattam as it was traditionally performed by Devadasis (female dancers) in temples (last surviving devadasi: R. Muthukannammal).
  • Symbolises: Fire.
  • It is found in Natya Shastra and is associated with Kalakshetra style.
  • It was banned by Britishers in 1910 but was later revived.
  • Revival by: E. Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale → renamed the dance Sadirattam to Bharatanatyam.

Forms of Classical Dance

  • Shaivite (majority) → Dedicated to Lord Shiva (masculine).
  • Vaishnavite → Dedicated to Lord Vishnu (feminine).
  • References in literature: Found in Silappatikaram (by Ilango Adigal) and Manimegalai (by Chithalai Chathanar).
  • Main mudra: Kataka Mukha Hasta.
  • Bharatanatyam was performed by certain families of the Tanjore district and these inheritors were known as 'Nattuvanar'.
  • Performance Style: Pandallur, Vazhuvoor, Kalakshetra, Melattur, Tanjore.
  • Movements/Stages of Dance: Alarippu (flowers offering), Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana, Mangalam.

Facts

  • Tamil text Tolkappiyam was composed during 2nd Sangam.
  • Lasya: Feminine (Parvati).
  • Tandava: Masculine (Shiva).
  • Bharatanatyam is also depicted in temple Gopuram (Chidambaram Temple).

Trick to Remember Exponents (Bharatanatyam)

भारत की अपनी मातृभूमि और उसने उतने ही अपनी माता स्वीकारी देवी के पंखन छुए और अपनी सुंदर डोले आलमोही और अपने सारे शस्त्रों को लेकर मातंगम वीर देवी पाठा भया और दल ताड़न यो भया।

Rukmini Devi Arundale

  • She is the first woman to be nominated in Rajya Sabha.
  • She is the founder of Kalakshetra Dance School (Estd. 1936).
  • She received: Padma Bhushan (1956).

Alarmel Valli is associated with Pandanallur style.

Yamini Krishnamurthi

  • "Asthana Narthaki" (Resident Dancer) title was bestowed upon her by Tirumala Tirupathi Devasthanam Temple.
  • She received: Padma Vibhushan (2016), Padma Bhushan (2001), Padma Shri (1968), Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1977).

Sonal Mansingh

  • She is the youngest recipient of Padma Vibhushan (2003).
  • Other Exponents: Rama Vaidyanathan, Meenakshi Chittaranjan, Narthaki Nataraj, Urmila Satyanarayanan, M. K. Saroja, Radha Sridhar, Deepak Mazumdar, C. V. Chandrashekhar.

Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh)

  • Earlier known as: Bhagavata Mela Dance (Tanjore, Tamil Nadu).
  • Modern form of dance is attributed to: Tirtha Narayanayati and Siddhendra Yogi [developed as a dance-drama → Bhama Kalpam (story of Satyabhama, the charming but jealous wife of Lord Krishna)].
  • Symbolises: Earth.
  • Elements: Ganesha Vandana, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Kalapam, Padam, Tarangam (it is the concluding part of dance where the dancer dances on a rim of brass plate).
  • Yakshagana was performed in Andhra Pradesh in earlier times. It is traditionally presented from dusk till dawn.

Trick (1) to Remember Exponents (Kuchipudi)

जिनके रूपवान में भी Reddy दिख जाए सब Kuchipudi से Related होगा।

  • Raja Reddy, Radha Reddy, Padmaja Reddy, Bhavana Reddy, Yamini Reddy.
  • Other Exponents: Yamini Krishnamurthy, Mallika Sarabhai.

माचा और सतीश लक्ष्मी जी की सत्यनारायण कथा में गए अब अरुणिम एक सुंदर लड़की शोभा के साथ कुचिपुड़ी पुत्री खबरें।

Odissi (Odisha)

  • Symbolises: Water.
  • Gotipua is a traditional dance form of Odisha that was originally performed by Maharis, female temple dancers. Today, young boys perform the dance in the style of the Maharis. Gotipua is the precursor to the classical Odissi dance.

Trick (1) to Remember (Odissi)

इसके बाद में Mohapatra और Mohanty दिख जाए तो Odissi से Related हैं।

  • Kelucharan Mohapatra (considered as father of Odissi who popularised the dance; Padma Vibhushan in 2000), Sujata Mohapatra, Leela Mohanty, Nharika Mohanty.
  • "Adiguru" of Odissi dance: Pankaj Charan Das.
  • Other Exponents: Kiran Sehgal, Mayadhar Raut, Indrani Rehman.
  • Protima Gauri founded Nrityagram (an institution in Karnataka) dance village and popularised Odissi.

Trick (2) to Remember Exponents (Odissi)

मुंडन के प्रधान माधवी से मिलने उड़ीशा आए और यह बात बिजय ने संजू और साहू को बता दी।

Elements in Odissi

Mangalacharan, Batu Nritya, Pallavi, Tharijham, Moksha.

Kathak (Uttar Pradesh)

  • The name is derived from "Katha" (storytelling).
  • It is the only classical dance to feature Persian elements. The Mughals patronised this dance.
  • It is performed in Hindustani music and Urdu ghazals.
  • The last Nawab of Awadh (Wajid Ali Shah) widely associated with the patronage of Kathak dance.
  • Elements: Amad, Thaat (standing position), Tukra, Paran, Jugalbandhi, Tarana, Bhaav, Kramalaya Ghat.
  • Gharanas associated with this dance: Lucknow Gharana (Founder: Ishwari Prasad), Jaipur Gharana (Founder: Bhanuji Maharaj), Banaras Gharana (Founder: Janaki Prasad).

Trick to Remember Exponents (Kathak)

श्रे महाराज बारायण और देवी में आरथा रखी उनका प्रसाद खात्रो विद्या मिलेगी लक्ष्मी प्रसाद बोलो और सब मंगल होगा।

Birju Maharaj

  • He is from Kalka Bindadin Gharana (Lucknow).
  • He founded the dance school Kalashram in Delhi in 1998.
  • Received: Padma Vibhushan (1986).
  • Other Exponents: Gopi Krishan, Rani Kasna, Geetanjali Lal, Maulik Shah.

Mohiniyattam (Kerala)

  • This dance form is associated with Hindu God Vishnu (his female avatar "Mohini").
  • This dance is also called "Dance of Enchanters" (graceful dance).
  • Symbolises: Air.
  • References of this dance is mentioned in "Vyavaharamala" (ancient text) written by Mazhamangalam Narayanan Namputiri.
  • This dance form has no abrupt jerks but has smooth performance.
  • This classical dance is known to have 24 hand gestures.
  • Elements: Cholkettu, Jatiswaram, Padavarnam, Padam, Tillana, Slokam, Saptam.
  • Dance Forms: Tevittichiyattam, Nangai Natakam, Dasiyattam.

Trick to Remember Exponents (Mohiniyattam)

मोहिनी गोपी के कान में सूँघा अब सारा कृष्णा की अम्मा।

Kalyanikutty Amma

  • She played a major role in revival of this dance form.
  • Received: Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1974).
  • She is the founder of Kerala Kalyanam (Estd. 1952).

V N Menon

  • He helped repeal the ban on temple dancing in Kerala thereby reviving the Mohiniyattam.
  • King Swathi Thirunnal not only revived Mohiniyattam, but was also responsible for inculcating Carnatic classical music into the dance form.

Kathakali (Kerala)

  • Katha means "Story" and Kali means "Performance".
  • This dance form is performed by a male performer. This dance is usually performed in temples after Sevakali session.
  • The vocal performance of this dance is in Sanskritised Malayalam.
  • It is based on epics of Ramayana and Mahabharata.
  • There is use of facial expressions and face colour (face is painted in green → the colour represents strength). Hence considered as "Mask Dance".
  • Colors and their meanings: Green (strength) and Red (evil).
  • Vesham (5), Expression (9), Hand gesture (24).
  • Forms: Natyam, Nritham, Nrithyam, Sangeetam, Vadya.
  • Elements: Kelikottu, Thodayam, Purappadu, Tiranokku, Ilakiyattam, Kalasam.
  • Aharya means costume and makeup in Sanskrit.
  • Kalaripayattu is a martial dance.

There are five major Veshams (makeup)

  • Pacha: Green, for noble, heroic, and generous characters.
  • Kathi: Knife, for villainous characters.
  • Thadi: Beard, for characters with beards.
  • Kari: Black, for evil characters.
  • Minukku: Radiant, for noble, virtuous female characters.
  • Pazhuppu (additional)

Manipuri (Manipur)

  • It is an introverted type of dance form which is based on Vaishnavism (a Vaishnavite form of dance).
  • Ashtapadis of Jayadeva's Gita Govinda are sung in Manipuri.

Forms of Manipuri Dance

  1. 1. Raas Leela
  • It depicts the love story of Krishna and Radha.
  • Propounder: Rajarshi Bhagya Chandra.
  1. 2. Sankirtana Tradition
  • Jagoi and Cholom are two parts of this tradition.
  • Cholom is masculine aspect of the dance form in which pung (drum) is used to perform the dances.
  1. 3. Thang-Ta
  • It is a martial dance.

Trick to Remember Exponents (Manipuri)

  • Surname with Devi is mostly associated with Manipuri dance: Kalavati Devi, Gambhini Devi, Bimbavati Devi.
  • Exponents: Jhaveri sisters, Nirmala Mehta, Guru Bipin Singh (He received the title "Hanjaba" from some Manipur King), Charu Mathur, Devyani Chalia, Aluna Kabuini.
  • Other Exponents: Rajkumar Singhajit Singh, Nileshwar Mukherjee.

Sattriya (Assam)

  • It is a Vaishnavite form of dance that was included under classical dance category in 2000.
  • The theme of dance form is related to Lord Krishna.
  • Founder of Sattriya Dance: Srimanta Sankaradeva.
  • Ankiya Naat is a "one-act play" written in Brajavali. In Assam, it is called as "Bhaona" a traditional art form that combines dance, music, and visual art.
  • Dance numbers: Chali (no theatre components), Jhumura, Nadu Bhangi.
  • Exponents: Jatin Goswami, Bhupen Hazarika (Bharat Ratna in 2019), Guru Ghanakanta Bora, Indira Bora, Maniram Dutta, Krishnakshi Kashyap, Meenakshi Medhi, Sharodi Saikia.

Various Organisations

  1. 1. Sangeet Natak Akademi / Indian National School of Dance: Delhi.
  2. 2. Kalakshetra School of Dance: Rukmini Devi Arundale (mother of Modern Bharatanatyam).
  3. 3. National Institute of Kathak: 1964 (New Delhi).
  4. 4. J Nehru Manipur Dance Academy: 1954 (Imphal).
  5. 5. Govindji Nrityalaya: Manipur.
  6. 6. Darpana Academy of Performing Arts established by Mrinalini Sarabhai and Vikram Sarabhai: 1949 (Ahmedabad).
  7. 7. Nalanda Nritya Kala Mahavidyalaya: Mumbai.
  8. 8. National Institute of Performing Arts: Mumbai.
  9. 9. Kalashram Kathak School established by Birju Maharaj: New Delhi.
  10. 10. Kadamb School of Dance and Music founded by Kumudini Lakhia: 1967 (Ahmedabad).

§ 5Verified and Edited 2025

Verification date: 2025-12-15

OCR Artifacts Fixed

  • No stray column separators, mojibake characters, or broken line breaks found in body text.

Factual Verifications

  • Bharatanatyam: Confirmed as oldest solo classical dance, associated with Natya Shastra, Kalakshetra, and Devadasis. Rukmini Devi Arundale's revival correctly attributed.
  • Kuchipudi: Confirmed Tirtha Narayanayati / Siddhendra Yogi origin and Bhama Kalpam connection.
  • Odissi: Confirmed Gotipua as precursor, Pankaj Charan Das as "Adiguru," and Kelucharan Mohapatra as "Father of Odissi" (Padma Vibhushan 2000).
  • Kathak: Confirmed Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras Gharanas with correct founders (Ishwari Prasad, Bhanuji Maharaj, Janaki Prasad).
  • Mohiniyattam: Confirmed 24 hand gestures, association with Vishnu's Mohini avatar, and Kalyanikutty Amma's revival role.
  • Kathakali: Confirmed green face paint (Pacha) representing strength, 5 Veshams, and 9 expressions.
  • Manipuri: Confirmed Rajarshi Bhagya Chandra as Raas Leela propounder; Vaishnavite tradition.
  • Sattriya: Confirmed Srimanta Sankaradeva as founder, included in classical dance category in 2000.
  • Padma Awards: Verified Birju Maharaj (Padma Vibhushan 1986), Yamini Krishnamurthy (Padma Vibhushan 2016), Sonal Mansingh (Padma Vibhushan 2003 — youngest), Rukmini Devi (Padma Bhushan 1956), Kalyanikutty Amma (Sangeet Natak Akademi 1974).
